title: Venkatesh Prasad Meets Karnataka CM, Focus On Restoring Top-Level Cricketing Action In Bengaluru | Cricket News - News18
text: Venkatesh Prasad, the newly elected president of the Karnataka State Cricket Association (KSCA), and his team initiated their efforts on Wednesday by visiting the KSCA Stadium in Belagavi. They also held discussions with Karnataka Chief Minister Siddaramaiah and Deputy Chief Minister DK Shivakumar to explore ways to reinstate top-level cricket at M Chinnaswamy Stadium. Prasad, accompanied by vice-president Sujith Somasundar and secretary Santosh Menon, assessed the condition of the KSCA Stadium in Belagavi. Veteran administrator Vinay Mruthyanjaya and KSCA Dharwad division’s convener Avinash Potdar were also part of the inspection team. The group deliberated on strategies to enhance cricket infrastructure throughout the state. “Belagavi, Shimoga, Tumakuru, Hubballi, and other centres will witness development in the coming days. Our focus is to rebuild cricket and revive the glory days for state cricket," Prasad stated following the visit. Prasad mentioned that the new KSCA administrators have already commenced discussions with CM Siddaramaiah, Deputy CM DK Shivakumar, and BCCI officials to bring top-flight cricket back to M Chinnaswamy Stadium. During the meeting, the newly elected KSCA Managing Committee, led by Venkatesh Prasad, pledged their full cooperation to the State Government. Prasad requested the CM and DCM to grant the necessary permissions to resume hosting cricket matches with spectators at the iconic M Chinnaswamy Stadium, aiming to restore high-level cricketing action to Bengaluru, according to a KSCA release. It is noteworthy that Women’s ODI World Cup matches were relocated from Bengaluru to other venues after the stadium failed to secure essential clearance from the authorities. The Chinnaswamy Stadium has not hosted any major matches since a stampede occurred near its premises, resulting in the tragic deaths of 11 fans during the Royal Challengers Bengaluru’s IPL victory celebration on June 4. The BCCI held the season-opening Duleep Trophy and India A’s two four-day matches against South Africa A at its Centre of Excellence
